newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Fire breaks out at Russian ammunition depot.
newsitem.headline: Fire breaks out at Russian ammunition depot.

text.p: An ammunition depot caught fire in Russia's Far East on Sunday, setting off a string of explosions and forcing the evacuation of a nearby village, an official said on Sunday.

No casualties were reported as a result of the fire, which broke out at an artillery depot six km (four miles) northwest of Bira at 0300 GMT, a spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry said by telephone.
Fragments of ammunition were blasted over a 12 km (seven mile) radius and shock waves blew out windows in some houses in Bira, whose 4,500 residents were evacuated.

The incident in the Jewish Autonomous Region on Russia's border with China was thought to have been sparked by a forest fire, but the possibility of sabotage was not being ruled out, Interfax news agency said.
The blasts, which began in the afternoon local time, continued into the night, Itar-Tass news agency reported later, saying the darkness and strong winds were hampering efforts to put out the fire.

Traffic was halted on a section of the Transsiberian Railway between the Bira and the regional centre Birobidzhan, but three fire-fighting trains and a passenger train to carry evacuees were sent to the area.
Officials declined to say how much ammunition was stored in the depot, which is at least the fourth to have caught fire in Russia over the past few years.
Tass said a forest fire had threatened another ammunition dump in the Far East on Sunday but that it had been put out before it reached the site.
